title: Strengthening the Mental Resilience of Our Young
what_it_is: Strengthening the Mental Resilience of Our Young

sections.label: Youth mental health study findings
sections.summary: The IMH National Youth Mental Health Study found one in three young people reported severe depression, anxiety or stress symptoms, with heavy social media use raising risk and nearly a third not seeking help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to the National Youth Mental Health Study conducted by the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) between 2022 and 2023, one in three young people reported experiencing severe or extremely severe symptoms of depression, anxiety or stress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Those who spent more than three hours daily on social media were especially at risk.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: And perhaps, most concerning of all, nearly a third of youths with severe symptoms do not seek help.

sections.label: Measuring mental resilience rigorously
sections.summary: The passage states that mental resilience must be measured with the same rigour as academic outcomes if it is to be taken seriously.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: If we are to take mental resilience seriously, we must measure it with the same rigour that we measure academic outcomes.

sections.label: National evidence framework for well-being
sections.summary: The passage states a charter could establish a national evidence framework for student well-being to strengthen accountability and learning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: To strengthen accountability and learning, the charter could establish a national evidence framework for student well-being.

sections.label: Charter pairing measurement with accreditation
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's charter could pair measurement with accreditation, with reviews considering peer support, counsellor accessibility and teacher readiness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Like the UK University's Mental Health Charter, Singapore's version could pair measurement with accreditation, where reviews consider indicators, such as the strength of peer support networks, perceive accessibility of counsellors and teacher readiness, to address mental well-being.

sections.label: MOE steps broadening success definition
sections.summary: The passage states MOE has taken steps through subject-based banding and applied learning pathways to broaden the definition of success.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: MOE has taken important steps – through subject-based banding and applied learning pathways – to broaden our definition of success.

sections.label: MOE-led School Mental Well-being Charter
sections.summary: The passage states an MOE-led School Mental Well-being Charter could unify the ecosystem, signalling priority, promoting consistency and encouraging innovation, co-led by MOE, HPB and IMH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: To bring this ecosystem to life, an MOE-led School Mental Well-being Charter could provide the unifying framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: It would serve three purposes: to signal national priority by recognising mental well-being as a core dimension of education; to promote consistency by setting minimum standards of psychological safety and resilience-building; and to encourage innovation, recognising schools that model excellence in student well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Charter could be co-led by MOE, HPB and IMH, rolled out across all school types, and supported by mentorship and peer-learning networks.

sections.label: Bridging policy and practice for resilience
sections.summary: The passage calls for bridging policy and practice to make resilience a lived reality and bouncing forward stronger and more connected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: Together, we can bridge policy and practice – supporting the MOE's efforts, sharing ground feedback and developing community-led initiatives that make resilience a lived reality, and not just a lesson plan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: In closing, Mr Speaker, let us remember that resilience is not just about bouncing back to where we were.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: It is about bouncing forward to become stronger, steadier and more connected.

sections.label: Mental Health Education in CCE curriculum
sections.summary: Mental Health Education lessons in the CCE curriculum cover automatic negative thoughts, emotional regulation, stress versus distress and help-seeking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Within the CCE curriculum, Mental Health Education lessons address topics such as the identifying and countering of automatic negative thoughts, emotional regulation, differentiating normal stress from distress and encouraging help-seeking habits.

sections.label: Empowering educators for student mental health support
sections.summary: Efforts empower educators with mental health literacy and counselling skills, referring students needing more support to school counsellors or community resources like REACH teams.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: There are ongoing efforts to empower educators to provide first-line support to our students, including raising their awareness, confidence and sensitivity to the growing and evolving mental health needs of our students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: We will continue to strengthen the mental health literacy of our educators through resources and professional development, including basic counselling skills and the ability to recognise students in distress.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Students who require more support are referred to school counsellors or community mental health resources, such as the Response Early intervention and Assessment in Community mental Health (REACH) teams in our hospitals such as the National University Hospital, IMH and KK Women's and Children's Hospital.

sections.label: Monitoring youth mental health through data
sections.summary: Youth mental health is monitored through data sources and research studies including the Youth Epidemiology and Resilience Study and the National Youth Mental Health Study.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Dr Chen also spoke about the importance of gathering data on student well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: We closely monitor the state of youth mental health through various data sources and research studies, including the recent Youth Epidemiology and Resilience Study by the National University of Singapore and the National Youth Mental Health Study by IMH.

sections.label: Termly student well-being check-in surveys
sections.summary: MOE conducts termly student well-being check-in surveys that enable teachers to detect struggling students and provide timely support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Yet another key approach that MOE has introduced is the student well-being check-in surveys conducted termly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: These surveys enable teachers to detect students who might be struggling and provide timely support.

sections.label: Systemic processes instead of Charter-based approach
sections.summary: The passage states that instead of a Charter-based approach, systemic processes have been instituted to achieve very similar outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Whilst we do not have a Charter-based approach suggested by the Member, we have instituted systemic processes to achieve very similar outcomes, as she has highlighted.

sections.label: School mental well-being Charter
sections.summary: The Member's call for a school mental well-being Charter is thanked and will be studied for feasibility, while skills and relationships are built.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: In closing, I want to thank the Member for the very rich ideas proposed in her call for a school mental well-being Charter, and we will study this carefully and explore its feasibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Rather, we seek to build up their skills, strengthen confidence in their knowledge base and develop the ability to form strong relationships so that they can view any difficult or challenging life circumstances through the lens of support, a weighted and healthy perspective as well as hope and optimism.
